response.title: what size electric generator do i need
response.answer:
The size of electric generator you need depends on what you want to power simultaneously and whether you're using it for home backup, an RV, or something else.

Generator sizes are measured in watts (W) or kilowatts (kW). 1 kW = 1,000 watts.

Typical generator sizes

Generator size

	

What it can power




1–2 kW

	

Phones, laptops, lights, small electronics




3–5 kW

	

Refrigerator, lights, Wi-Fi, TV, small appliances




5–8 kW

	

Essential home circuits, some larger appliances




8–12 kW

	

Most home essentials, potentially a small AC




12–20 kW

	

Many household appliances and central AC




20–26+ kW

	

Whole-house backup for many homes

These are approximate ranges. Electric heating, air conditioning, water heaters, and EV charging can significantly increase the required capacity.

Calculate your generator size

Select the appliances you want to run at the same time:

Refrigerator

700 W

Freezer

500 W

Lights

200 W

Wi-Fi and electronics

200 W

Microwave

1,200 W

Sump pump

1,000 W

Window AC

1,200 W

Central AC (approx. 3 ton)

3,500 W

Electric water heater

4,500 W

Electric stove/oven

3,000 W

Running load

1,100 W

Estimated peak load

2,400 W

Suggested generator running capacity

3.0 kW
Preliminary estimate with 20% headroom and one major startup surge. Actual motor startup requirements and generator surge ratings vary.

One question: Are you sizing a generator for your entire house, just essential appliances during a power outage, or something else?

If it's for your house, I can help you calculate a more accurate size based on your AC, heating, and major appliances. Also, never run a fuel-powered generator indoors or connect it to house wiring without an approved transfer switch or interlock.
markup:
The size of electric generator you need depends on **what you want to power simultaneously** and whether you're using it for home backup, an RV, or something else.

Generator sizes are measured in **watts (W)** or **kilowatts (kW)**. 1 kW = 1,000 watts.

## Typical generator sizes

| Generator size | What it can power |
|---|---|
| 1–2 kW | Phones, laptops, lights, small electronics |
| 3–5 kW | Refrigerator, lights, Wi-Fi, TV, small appliances |
| 5–8 kW | Essential home circuits, some larger appliances |
| 8–12 kW | Most home essentials, potentially a small AC |
| 12–20 kW | Many household appliances and central AC |
| 20–26+ kW | Whole-house backup for many homes |

These are approximate ranges. Electric heating, air conditioning, water heaters, and EV charging can significantly increase the required capacity.

## Calculate your generator size

{@body const appliances = [{name:"Refrigerator",w:700,s:2000},{name:"Freezer",w:500,s:1500},{name:"Lights",w:200,s:200},{name:"Wi-Fi and electronics",w:200,s:200},{name:"Microwave",w:1200,s:1200},{name:"Sump pump",w:1000,s:2500},{name:"Window AC",w:1200,s:3000},{name:"Central AC (approx. 3 ton)",w:3500,s:9000},{name:"Electric water heater",w:4500,s:4500},{name:"Electric stove/oven",w:3000,s:3000}]}
{@body const [selected,setSelected] = DIL.useState([0,2,3])}
{@body const running=selected.reduce((sum,i)=>sum+appliances[i].w,0)}
{@body const peak=selected.length?running+Math.max(...selected.map(i=>appliances[i].s-appliances[i].w)):0}
{@body const recommended=Math.ceil(peak*1.2/500)*500}
<box border radius="2xl" padding={3} gap={3}>
  <text weight="medium">Select the appliances you want to run at the same time:</text>
  <box gap={2}>
    {#each appliances as a,i}
      <row key={a.name} align="center" justify="between">
        <checkbox checked={selected.includes(i)} onChange={v=>setSelected(old=>v?[...old,i]:old.filter(x=>x!==i))} lineThrough={false}>{a.name}</checkbox>
        <text color="secondary" size="xs" tabularNums>{a.w.toLocaleString()} W</text>
      </row>
    {/each}
  </box>
  <divider color="subtle"/>
  <grid columns={2} gap={2}>
    <grid-item>
      <text color="secondary" size="xs">Running load</text>
      <title size="lg" tabularNums>{running.toLocaleString()} W</title>
    </grid-item>
    <grid-item>
      <text color="secondary" size="xs">Estimated peak load</text>
      <title size="lg" tabularNums>{peak.toLocaleString()} W</title>
    </grid-item>
  </grid>
  <box background="surface-secondary" radius="lg" padding={3} gap={1}>
    <text color="secondary" weight="medium" size="xs">Suggested generator running capacity</text>
    <title size="2xl" color="default" tabularNums>{selected.length?(recommended/1000).toFixed(1)+" kW":"—"}</title>
    <caption>Preliminary estimate with 20% headroom and one major startup surge. Actual motor startup requirements and generator surge ratings vary.</caption>
  </box>
</box>

**One question:** Are you sizing a generator for your **entire house**, just **essential appliances during a power outage**, or something else?

If it's for your house, I can help you calculate a more accurate size based on your AC, heating, and major appliances. Also, never run a fuel-powered generator indoors or connect it to house wiring without an approved transfer switch or interlock.
